You are a statistical geneticist. You are given a GWAS summary-statistics file that may or may not contain data-integrity / QC problems. Determine whether these summary statistics can be TRUSTED for downstream analysis (e.g. TWAS), and what would need to be fixed first.

Dataset path: /tmp/gwsbx_2loj5gxc/cell022.tsv.gz   (tab-separated, gzip-compressed; one row per variant)
Its directory may contain additional files describing the dataset.

You have a Python sandbox: call run_python(code). The dataframe is preloaded as `df` (pandas as pd, numpy as np, scipy.stats as stats; statsmodels/sklearn importable); you may also read other files in the dataset's directory. Only text you print is returned; plots are NOT rendered.

Record EVERY check you run in `trajectory` (including checks that turned up nothing). Then return ONLY this JSON:
{"issues_found": [{"description": "<what is wrong, in your words, or 'none'>",
                    "affected_entities": ["<id / coordinate / column, if identifiable>"],
                    "action": "<what you would do about it, or 'none'>"}],
 "issue_present_probability": <0-1>,
 "analysis_usable": <true|false>,
 "trajectory": [{"step": "<what you examined>", "finding": "<what you found>", "action": "<concluded/did>"}]}
